account:
It is day 0, just after eleven, and I am at the plaza following my ten o'clock market walk. So far the town appears to be conducting ordinary business. The secretary reports no urgent correspondence. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later bread near the bridge and inn. I saw the baker carrying a sack of bread toward the west bank, and now see the baker near the market stall. The neighbour says the baker promised fresh bread at the stall today. This looks consistent with preparing and delivering the day's bread; I have no evidence of anything unusual about it.

The builder asked whether I had seen the innkeeper or freight operator, saying there were supplies to discuss. I have not learned which supplies or whether there is any actual shortage. The builder has walked away, possibly to pursue those conversations, but I do not know the destination or purpose beyond the stated supply discussion.

The neighbour confirmed our three o'clock tea at the east-bank cottage, road point (16, -60, 105), beside the ferry. The secretary is trying to clarify the same directions for the appointment book. My recent replies sometimes registered as unheard despite people appearing nearby, so I should not assume that my explanations reached them. My remaining appointments today are lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, tea at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven. Nothing I have observed yet establishes an emergency or a concealed undertaking.
